case_name: Ashok Walia and Anr. v. State of Himachal Pradesh and Ors.

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Ashok Walia and Anr., husband and wife
parties.respondent_defendant: State of Himachal Pradesh and Ors.

facts_of_case: Petitioners' marriage was solemnized on 23.2.2023, but they started harassing the complainant for bringing lesser dowry. She left her matrimonial house and started living with her parents w.e.f. 26.5.2023. FIR No. 27/23 was registered under Sections 498-A, 504 and 506 of IPC.

legal_principles.principle: Power under S. 482 CrPC is not to be exercised in cases which involve heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc.
legal_principles.held: Such offences are not private in nature and have a serious impact on society.
cited_cases: Narinder Singh and others versus State of Punjab and another, (2014)6 SCC 466

legal_principles.principle: Power to quash criminal proceedings under S. 482 CrPC is to be exercised sparingly and with great caution.
legal_principles.held: This power is to be exercised sparingly and with great caution.
cited_cases: Narinder Singh and others versus State of Punjab and another, (2014)6 SCC 466

legal_principles.principle: Offences committed under special statute like the Prevention of Corruption Act or by Public Servants while working in that capacity are not to be quashed merely on the basis of compromise between the victim and the offender.
legal_principles.held: Apart from this, offences committed under special statute like the Prevention of Corruption Act or the offences committed by Public Servants while working in that capacity are not to be quashed merely on the basis of compromise between the victim and the offender.
cited_cases: Narinder Singh and others versus State of Punjab and another, (2014)6 SCC 466
use_in: cases involving special statutes or Public Servants

legal_principles.principle: Criminal cases having overwhelmingly and predominantly civil character, particularly arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes may be quashed when the parties have resolved their entire disputes among themselves.
legal_principles.held: Those criminal cases having overwhelmingly and predominantly civil character, particularly arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes may be quashed when the parties have resolved their entire disputes among themselves.
cited_cases: Narinder Singh and others versus State of Punjab and another, (2014)6 SCC 466

outcome.final_order: FIR No. 27/23 sought to be quashed on the basis of compromise/amicable settlement arrived inter-se parties.
